title: 1971 AHSME Problem 33
statement: If \(P\) is the product of \(n\) quantities in geometric progression, \(S\) their sum, and \(S'\) the sum of their reciprocals, then \(P\) in terms of \(S,\) \(S',\) and \(n\) is:

solutions.text:
Write the terms as \(a,ar,\ldots,ar^{n-1}.\) Reversing the reciprocal sum gives \[ S'=\frac{S}{a^2r^{n-1}}, \] so \(\frac{S}{S'}=a^2r^{n-1}.\) Meanwhile \[ \begin{aligned} P&=a^nr^{\frac{n(n-1)}{2}}\\ &=\left(a^2r^{n-1}\right)^{\frac{n}{2}}\\ &=\left(\frac{S}{S'}\right)^{\frac{n}{2}}. \end{aligned} \]

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
